# One claim-payload directive, in a fan-out and out of it

`{{claim.<alias>.payload}}` reads the producer's payload for the claim the node
holds. Inside a fan-out, the same directive reads each sub-claim's own payload.
There is one directive to learn, not two.

## The deployment

Two pick policies, each supplying a payload per claimed item:

```yaml
root: /workspace
host: 127.0.0.1
grpc_port: 9200
http_port: 9210
sweep_interval_seconds: 60
pick_policies:
  "@single":
    root: "single"
    on_commit: recycle
    on_give_up: recycle
    visibility_timeout_seconds: 60
    sync_strategy: on_open
  "@batch":
    root: "batch"
    on_commit: recycle
    on_give_up: recycle
    visibility_timeout_seconds: 60
    sync_strategy: on_open
```

## The template

Two nodes with byte-identical attribute sources, differing only in how the claim
arrives.

```yaml
name: sub-claim-payload-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: direct
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    claim_producers:
      - name: claim-producer-filesystem
        selector: "@single"
        intent: rw
        alias: q
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          folder: {type: string, source: "{{claim.q.payload.folder}}"}
          whole:  {type: object, source: "{{claim.q.payload}}"}

  - type: fanned
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    claim_producers:
      - name: claim-producer-filesystem
        selector: "@batch"
        intent: rw
        alias: q
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
    fan_out:
      claim: q
      partition_request: '{"batch_pick": {"max_items": 3}}'
      parallelism: 3
      error_policy:
        kind: best_effort
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          folder: {type: string, source: "{{claim.q.payload.folder}}"}
          whole:  {type: object, source: "{{claim.q.payload}}"}
```

## What the product does

**On the regular claim.** The field path resolves to that claim's payload field,
and the bare path resolves to the whole payload object.

**In the fan-out.** Three sub-claims are opened, and each clone settles carrying
the payload of its own sub-claim: the set of resolved `folder` values equals the
set of sub-claim partition keys, no two clones resolve the same value, and the
bare path resolves to the same object whose field the field path returned.

The resolved attribute shape is identical in both contexts, and the parent and
all three clones settle fresh.
